name: cahute
desc: Library and set of utilities to interact with Casio calculators
why: Talks to Casio calculators over their serial protocol, a rare hardware door into old calculator link formats and transfer internals.

brief.what_it_is: Cahute is a C library and a set of command-line utilities for talking to CASIO calculators over their serial and USB protocols and reading or writing the file formats those calculators use. Per the homepage, it covers file transfer to and from calculator storage (p7), program backup from calculators from 1991 onward (CaS), text-encoding conversion (cahute_convert_text()), screen capture and screenstreaming to the host (p7screen), and ROM flashing for fx-9860G and compatible models (p7os). The executables listed in the package metadata are p7, p7os, p7screen and xfer9860. The homepage itself is the Diátaxis-style documentation site for version 0.6.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes the project as a library and utility set for CASIO calculators dating from the 1990s to today, and credits earlier reverse-engineering work by others (CaS, Caspro, Casetta, fxReverse, xfer9860, UsbConnector, and the Cemetech Prizm Wiki) as the basis it was built on. It does not state a single explicit motivation beyond that.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage documents a set of serial and USB protocols by calculator generation (CASIOLINK, CAS40, CAS50, CAS100, CAS300, and Protocol 7.00 for post fx-9860G models), along with a USB Mass Storage transport. The tools speak these protocols to a connected calculator, and the library exposes concepts such as links, mediums, contexts and files. The homepage does not go into more mechanism than that.
brief.install_notes: Officially supported platforms per the homepage: Arch Linux and derivatives (install from the AUR, install via GiteaPC, or build natively) and macOS / OS X (install with Homebrew, or build natively). Debian, Void Linux, Microsoft Windows (Visual Studio for Vista+ and XP, or MinGW-w64) and AmigaOS (built from Linux) are listed as in progress or awaiting volunteers. The docs include a Windows USB drivers page and a Wireshark USB-capture guide. The homepage does not show any first-run or configuration steps, and I did not open the install pages.
brief.standout: It is a rare open reimplementation that talks to CASIO calculators across roughly three decades of hardware, from CAS40 through Protocol 7.00, and it documents the wire protocols in detail on its site. Most of the other tools in this space cover only one protocol generation.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as the homepage shows. It is labelled version 0.6, the homepage says the project is maintained by Thomas Touhey and is being worked on on GitLab, and the docs cover release and packaging processes. I did not find a release date or last-commit date on the homepage, so I cannot give a more precise date.
brief.caveats: Officially supported platforms are only Arch Linux and derivatives and macOS. Debian, Void, Windows and AmigaOS are described as in progress or awaiting volunteers. The project's code and documentation are licensed under CeCILL 2.1. The documentation icons come from the Mutant Standard under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, which is a non-commercial share-alike licence and differs from the code licence. The homepage does not describe what a calculator needs to be connected or set up, and it was the only page I read, so I did not check the command reference or install guides. Because the homepage does not show command lines, commands_seen is empty.
quotes: Cahute is a library and set of command-line utilities to handle serial and USB communication protocols and file formats related to CASIO calculators, dating from the 1990s to today.
With CaS, extract programs from all CASIO calculators since 1991, over USB and serial links!
With p7, transfer files from and to storages on fx-9860G compatible calculators, over USB and serial links!
It is maintained by Thomas Touhey.
fetch_log: https://cahute.org/ : fetched successfully. It is a documentation site, not a GitHub README. It lists the install, build, command-line, protocol and reference sections but does not include the sub-pages, so I did not follow any further links.
